--- title: "Vocabulary: definitions" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · L_ORAL_SEM_VOCABULARIO_DEFINICIONES" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (A · Accuracy; quality class A). Generated on November 27, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea L_ORAL_SEM_VOCABULARIO_DEFINICIONES`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Vocabulario: definiciones*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/L_ORAL_SEM_VOCABULARIO_DEFINICIONES.html). ::: **In one sentence.** Vocabulary: definitions, from age 4 to 5 (2,162 administrations in 3 cohorts). AUC .60–.68 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 1705 | | Battery | BUIZA | | Format | forced choice | | Items | 20 (1705) according to the platform | | Task family | A · Accuracy | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | The child describes the meaning of 20 words. | ## How it is programmed on the platform The platform is the reference: what the activity actually presents is what is measured. Configuration read from the activity itself on 23/10/2026 (without modifying it). Cell contents are in Spanish. | Code|Name on the platform |Presentation | Test items| Practice items|Example items |Time limit |Order |Scoring | Age.term (label 3)| |----:|:--------------------|:------------------------------------------------------------|----------:|--------------:|:-------------|:----------|:-----|:--------|------------------------:| | 1705|Vocabulario |Un estímulo por pantalla; el evaluador marca acierto o error | 20| 0|— |— |fijo |Aciertos | 4, 4.3, 5, 5.1, 5.2, 5.3| **Differences from the dictionary or the instructions (in Spanish):** - **1705.** Definiciones de 20 palabras con ejemplos de respuesta válida para el evaluador (proyecto BUIZA): comprobar la autoría antes de publicar ítems. *Age.term: provisional reading of the activity's label 3 (3rd digit = age, 4th = term; 0 = annual), to be confirmed with the engineer.* **How it looks on the platform** (first item or example; 2026 screenshot; the interface is in Spanish). ::: {layout-ncol=1} ![1705 · Vocabulario](../../figuras/plataforma/1705.jpg){.lightbox width="40%" fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 1705"} ::: ## Theoretical framework Vocabulary is knowledge of word meanings. The platform measures it in two ways: **orally**, when the child explains the meaning of a word they hear, and **through reading**, when they choose, among three written words, the one with a similar meaning. In the simple view of reading, vocabulary is part of language comprehension, the component that does not depend on reading [@hoover1990simple]. **What the evidence says:** - **Preschool oral language predicts reading comprehension years later.** Comprehension at age 8½ is explained by word reading at 5 and by language at 3½, in children at family risk of dyslexia and in the rest [@hulme2015foundations]. Language in the broad sense (vocabulary, grammar, inference) predicts it better than vocabulary alone [@lervag2018comprehension]. - **Written vocabulary is not only language.** Vocabulary tasks also capture variance from decoding, because the meaning, written form and phonology of each word are connected [@protopapas2013vocabulary]. - **The relation is reciprocal.** Reading more expands vocabulary, and a larger vocabulary makes it easier to read new words [@killingly2024reciprocal]. In the first school years the code (letters and phonological awareness) weighs more; later, word reading and comprehension separate [@storch2002oral]. **What our data show.** Vocabulary through reading predicts low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency almost as well as the reading tasks (median AUC .75), but it is not very stable between terms (ρ = .43). Oral vocabulary at ages 4 and 5 has good internal consistency (α = .82) and predicts less (median AUC .63, maximum .71). This is to be expected: its main role is in comprehension, not fluency. It is also one of the best predictors of arithmetic at ages 10–11 ([Numerical cognition](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/cognicion-numerica.html#sec-mate-criterio), *in Spanish*). ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 4.1| 2013| 181|2017/18 | 577| 569| 8| 24| | 4.2| 2011| 131|2015/16 | 799| 0| 799| 33| | 5.2| 2010| 130|2015/16 | 786| 255| 530| 35| | Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----------:|---:|-------:|-----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 4.1| 569| 2013| 10.41| 4.09| 11| -0.52| 2.46| 0.18| | 5.2| 255| 2010| 11.78| 3.97| 12| -0.44| 1.18| 1.96| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). The usual range goes from P1 to P99 (98% of the children). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning; the possible range is 0–20 correct responses. | Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. |Possible range | Warning| |----------:|---:|:--------------------|:---------|:--------------|-------:| | 4.1| 569|0–18 |0–20 |0–20 | | | 5.2| 255|1.1–20 |0–20 |0–20 | | ## Reliability There are no two time points with the same children (at least 80). α (2021) = .81. ## Validity **Concurrent.** Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Oral morphosyntax (4.1, r = .41); Phonological awareness (4.2, r = .44); Phonological awareness (5.2, r = .43). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .60–.68. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .57–.64. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_L_ORAL_SEM_VOCABULARIO_DEFINICIONES_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .53–.71 (3 time points; 122–221 children). ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|---:|-------:|--:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4.1| 569| 2013| 2| 5.0| 6| 8| 11| 13| 15| | 4.2| 799| 2011| 4| 5.0| 7| 8| 11| 14| 16| | 5.2| 255| 2010| 5| 6.4| 8| 9| 12| 14| 17| These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_L_ORAL_SEM_VOCABULARIO_DEFINICIONES_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|---:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 4.1| 577| 0.043| 0.304| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 4.1| 575| 0.072| 0.390| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 4.1| 576| 0.142| 0.001| |School (ICC) | 4.1| 577| 0.246| | |School SES (ρ) | 4.2| 799| 0.237| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 4.2| 772| -0.087| 0.227| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 4.2| 767| 0.134| 0.000| |School (ICC) | 4.2| 799| 0.227| | |School SES (ρ) | 5.2| 786| 0.254| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 5.2| 749| -0.159| 0.030| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 5.2| 748| 0.114| 0.002| |School (ICC) | 5.2| 786| 0.275| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Vocabulary: definitions” (code 1705; BUIZA battery) assesses expressive vocabulary. The child selects a response among the options presented on the screen. It comprises 20 items. The time limit is 150 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2011 and 2013 cohorts it was administered in 3 sessions, from 4 to 5 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. In our data (2021 analyses), internal consistency was α = .81 (N = 580, 20 items). Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .57–.64. ## Pending issues - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
